 18052                                  
 18053                                  int02:
 18054                                  
 18055                                  ; *********************************************************************
 18056                                  ;
 18057                                  ; this is special support for the pc convertible / nmi handler
 18058                                  ;
 18059                                  ;	on the pc convertible, there is a situation where an nmi can be 
 18060                                  ;	caused by using the "out" instructions to certain ports. when this
 18061                                  ;	occurs, the pc convertible hardware *guarantees* that **nothing** 
 18062                                  ;	can stop the nmi or interfere with getting to the nmi handler. this
 18063                                  ;	includes other type of interrupts (hardware and software), and
 18064                                  ;	also includes other type of nmi's. when any nmi has occured,
 18065                                  ;	no other interrtupt (hardware, software or nmi) can occur until
 18066                                  ;	the software takes specific steps to allow further interrupting.
 18067                                  ;
 18068                                  ;	for pc convertible, the situation where the nmi is generated by the
 18069                                  ;	"out" to a control port requires "fixing-up" and re-attempting. in
 18070                                  ;	otherwords, it is actually a "restartable exception". in this
 18071                                  ;	case, the software handler must be able to get to the stack in
 18072                                  ;	order to figure out what instruction caused the problem, where
 18073                                  ;	it was "out"ing to and what value it was "out"ing.  therefore,
 18074                                  ;	we will not switch stacks in this situation. this situation is
 18075                                  ;	detected by interrogating port 62h, and checking for a bit value
 18076                                  ;	of 80h. if set, *****do not switch stacks*****.
 18077                                  ;
 18078                                  ; *********************************************************************
 18079

 18081 00000017 06                      	push	es

 18092                                  				; 6: 1=I/O channel check
 18093                                  				; 7: 1=RAM parity check error occurred.

 18332                                  ;********************************************************************
 18333                                  
 18334                                  ; do interrupt stack switching. the fake return address holds
 18335                                  ; a pointer to the far-pointer of the actual interrupt
 18336                                  ; service routine
 18337                                  
 18338                                  ; 21/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 18339                                  ; 21/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 18340                                  
 18341                                  ;allocbyte   equ 0
 18342                                  ;intlevel    equ 1
 18343                                  ;savedsp     equ 2
 18344                                  ;savedss     equ 4
 18345                                  ;newsp       equ 6
 18346                                  
 18347                                  ; 30/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.2 (Modified MSDOS 6.21 SYSINIT)
 18348                                  ; (MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS, SYSINIT:0147h)
 18349                                  
 18350                                  do_int_stacks:
 18351 00000147 50                      	push	ax
 18352 00000148 55                      	push	bp
 18353 00000149 06                      	push	es

 18355 0000014F 2E8B2E[1000]            	mov	bp,[cs:nextentry]	; get most likely candidate
 18356 00000154 B001                    	mov	al,allocated ; 1
 18357                                  	; 21/10/2022
 18358                                  	;xchg	[es:bp+allocbyte],al 
 18359                                  	; 11/12/2022
 18360 00000156 26864600                	xchg	[es:bp],al		; grab the entry
 18361 0000015A 3C00                    	cmp	al,free ; 0		; still avail?
 18362 0000015C 7551                    	jne	short notfree02
 18363                                  
 18364 0000015E 2E832E[1000]08          	sub	word [cs:nextentry],entrysize ; set for next interrupt
 18365                                  
 18366                                  found02:
 18367 00000164 26896602                	mov	[es:bp+savedsp],sp	; save sp value
 18368 00000168 268C5604                	mov	[es:bp+savedss],ss	; save ss also

 18371

 18373                                  	; 21/10/2022

 18376                                  	;cmp	[es:bp+0],ax

 18378 00000176 7544                    	jne	short foundbad02

 18380                                  	; 02/07/2023 (MSDOS 6.21 SYSINIT code)

 19798                                  ; It will either be relocated to low memory, above the DOS data structures,
 19799                                  ; or else it will be located in HiMem, in which case a stub with the DOS
 19800                                  ; code entry points will be located in low memory. Dos_segreinit is used
 19801                                  ; to tell the DOS data where the code has been placed, and to install the
 19802                                  ; low memory stub if necessary. If the DOS is going to go into HiMem, we
 19803                                  ; must first initialize it in its present location and load the installable
 19804                                  ; device drivers. Then, if a HiMem driver has been located, we can actually
 19805                                  ; relocate the DOS code into HiMem.
 19806                                  ;
 19807                                  ; For ROMDOS, if DOS=HIGH is indicated, then we need to call dos_segreinit
 19808                                  ; to install the low memory stub (this must be done before allowing any
 19809                                  ; device drivers to hook interrupt vectors). Otherwise, we don't need to 
 19810                                  ; call dos_segreinit at all, since the interrupt vector table has already 
 19811                                  ; been patched.

 20148                                  ; we are going to open the command interpreter and size it as is done in
 20149                                  ; ldfil. the reason we must do this is that sysinit is in free memory. if
 20150                                  ; there is not enough room for the command interpreter,exec will probably
 20151                                  ; overlay our stack and code so when it returns with an error sysinit won't be
 20152                                  ; here to catch it. this code is not perfect (for instance .exe command
 20153                                  ; interpreters are possible) because it does its sizing based on the
 20154                                  ; assumption that the file being loaded is a .com file. it is close enough to
 20155                                  ; correctness to be usable.

 20186                                  ; anyway, and no one has responsibility for freeing "config_wrkseg". But
 20187                                  ; we need to make sure that there's no way Exec will stomp on that data
 20188                                  ; before it can copy it, and one way to do that is to make the available
 20189                                  ; memory calculation even more "paranoid", by subtracting "config_wrkseg"
 20190                                  ; from the "memory_size" segment value (which is typically A000h) instead
 20191                                  ; of the current sysinit CS....

 20194                                  ; slid the data required by Exec up to the very top of memory, because as
 20195                                  ; it stands, you have to have sizeof(COMMAND.COM) PLUS 64K to load just
 20196                                  ; COMMAND.COM (64k is about what sysinit, and all the goop above sysinit,
 20197                                  ; consumes). Now it's just a little worse (65K or more, depending on
 20198                                  ; the size of your CONFIG.SYS, since the size of the environment workspace
 20199                                  ; is determined by the size of CONFIG.SYS.... -JTP

 21049                                  ; BUGBUG -- 5 Aug 92 -- chuckst -- Allocating space for DOS
 21050                                  ;	  using DOS itself causes an arena to be generated.
 21051                                  ;	  Unfortunately, certain programs (like PROTMAN$)
 21052                                  ;	  assume that the device drivers are loaded into
 21053                                  ;	  the first arena. For this reason, MagicDrv's
 21054                                  ;	  main device driver header arena is manually
 21055                                  ;	  truncated from the arena chain, and the space
 21056                                  ;	  for DOS is allocated using the following
 21057                                  ;	  simple code, which also assumes that the
 21058                                  ;	  first arena is the free one where DOS's low
 21059                                  ;	  stub will go.
 21060                                  ;
 21061                                  ; M012 : BEGIN
 21062                                  
 21063                                  	; 23/10/2022
 21064                                  update_arena:

 21066 00000A01 57                      	push	di
 21067 00000A02 51                      	push	cx
 21068 00000A03 52                      	push	dx

 21070                                  	;lds	di,[cs:DOSINFO]			; get ptr to DOS var
 21071                                  	; 11/12/2022
 21072                                  	; ds = cs 
 21073 00000A04 C53E[6D02]              	lds	di,[DOSINFO] ; 27/03/2019	
 21074 00000A08 4F                      	dec	di
 21075 00000A09 4F                      	dec	di				; Arena head is immediately
 21076                                  						;  before sysvar
 21077 00000A0A 8E05                    	mov	es,[di]				; es = arena head
 21078                                  	;mov	cx,[es:ARENA.SIZE]		; cx = total low mem size
 21079 00000A0C 268B0E0300              	mov	cx,[es:3]
 21080 00000A11 39D9                    	cmp	cx,bx				; is it sufficient ?
 21081 00000A13 7227                    	jb	short FatalErr			; no, fatal error
 21082                                  
 21083                                  	;mov	dl,[es:ARENA.SIGNATURE]
 21084 00000A15 268A160000              	mov	dl,[es:0]
 21085 00000A1A 8CC0                    	mov	ax,es
 21086 00000A1C 01D8                    	add	ax,bx				; ax = new arena head
 21087 00000A1E 8905                    	mov	[di],ax				; store it in DOS data area
 21088 00000A20 8ED8                    	mov	ds,ax
 21089                                  	;mov	[ARENA.SIGNATURE],dl		; type of arena
 21090 00000A22 88160000                	mov	[0],dl

 21296                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 21297                                  ;
 21298                                  ; following piece of code will be moved into a para boundary. And the para
 21299                                  ; address posted in seg of int 19h vector. Offset of int 19h will point to
 21300                                  ; VDint19. This is to protect HMA from apps which use VDISK header method
 21301                                  ; to determine free extended memory.
 21302                                  ;
 21303                                  ; For more details read "power programming" column by Ray Duncan in the
 21304                                  ; May 30 1989 issue of PC Magazine (pp 377-388) [USING EXTENDED MEMORY,PART 1]
 21305                                  ;
 21306                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 21307                                  
 21308                                  StartVDHead:
 21309                                  ;-------------- what follows is a dummy device driver header (not used by DOS)
 21310                                  
 21311 00000AC0 00000000                	dd	0		; link to next device driver
 21312 00000AC4 0080                    	dw	8000h		; device attribute
 21313 00000AC6 0000                    	dw	0		; strategy routine offset
 21314 00000AC8 0000                    	dw	0		; interrupt routine offset
 21315 00000ACA 01                      	db	1		; number of units
 21316                                  	;db	7 dup(0) 
 21317 00000ACB 00<rep 7h>              	times	7 db 0 		; reserved area
 21318                                  VDiskSig1:
 21319 00000AD2 564449534B              	db	'VDISK'
 21320                                  
 21321                                  VLEN1	equ	($-VDiskSig1)
 21322                                  
 21323 00000AD7 202056332E33            	db	'  V3.3'	; vdisk label
 21324                                  	;db	15 dup (0)	; pad
 21325 00000ADD 00<rep Fh>              	times	15 db 0
 21326 00000AEC 0000                    	dw	0		; bits 0-15 of free HMA
 21327 00000AEE 11                      	db	11h		; bits 16-23 of free HMA (1M + 64K)
 21328                                  VDInt19:
 21329 00000AEF EA                      	db	0EAh		; jmp to old vector
 21330                                  OldVDInt19:
 21331 00000AF0 00000000                	dd	0		; Saved int 19 vector
 21332                                  
 21333                                  EndVDHead: ; label byte
 21334                                  
 21335                                  VDiskHMAHead:	
 21336 00000AF4 000000                  	db	0,0,0		; non-bootable disk
 21337                                  VDiskSig2:
 21338 00000AF7 564449534B              	db	'VDISK'
 21339                                  
 21340                                  VLEN2	equ	($-VDiskSig2)
 21341                                  
 21342 00000AFC 332E33                  	db	'3.3'		; OEM - signature
 21343 00000AFF 8000                    	dw	128		; number of bytes/sector
 21344 00000B01 01                      	db	1		; sectors/cluster
 21345 00000B02 0100                    	dw	1		; reserved sectors
 21346 00000B04 01                      	db	1		; number of FAT copies
 21347 00000B05 4000                    	dw	64		; number of root dir entries
 21348 00000B07 0002                    	dw	512		; number of sectors
 21349 00000B09 FE                      	db	0FEh		; media descriptor
 21350 00000B0A 0600                    	dw	6		; number of sectors/FAT
 21351 00000B0C 0800                    	dw	8		; sectors per track
 21352 00000B0E 0100                    	dw	1		; number of heads
 21353 00000B10 0000                    	dw	0		; number of hidden sectors
 21354 00000B12 4004                    	dw	440h		; Start of free HMA in K (1M+64K)
 21355                                  
 21356                                  EndVDiskHMAHead: ; label byte

 21507                                  ;; is set. On those machines the INT 15h block move code	      ;I070
 21508                                  ;; goes through the 8042 to twiddle A20 instead of port 92h.	      ;I070
 21509                                  ;; In password server mode the 8042 is disabled so the block	      ;I070
 21510                                  ;; move crashes the system. We can do this because these	      ;I070
 21511                                  ;; systems clear all of memory on a cold boot.			      ;I070

 21517                                  ;               cmp     word [cs:sys_model_byte],19F8h                ;I070
 21518                                  ;               je      short ClrVDISKno                              ;I070
 21519                                  ;                                      ; Check for mod 30-286	      ;I070
 21520                                  ;               cmp     word [cs:sys_model_byte],09FCh                ;I070

 23008                                  ;
 23009                                  ;	ParaRound rounds a byte count up to a multiple of 16, then divides
 23010                                  ;	by 16 yielding a "length in paragraphs" value.

 23024                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 23025                                  ; sysinit_base module.
 23026                                  ;
 23027                                  ; This module is relocated by the routine EndFile to a location in low
 23028                                  ; memory. It is then called by SYSINIT to perform the EXEC of programs
 23029                                  ; that are being loaded by the "install=" command. After the EXEC call
 23030                                  ; completes, this module performs a checksum on the SYSINIT code (at the
 23031                                  ; top of memory) to be sure that the EXECed program did not damage it.
 23032                                  ; If it did, then this module will print an error message and stop the
 23033                                  ; system. Otherwise, it returns control to SYSINIT.
 23034                                  ;
 23035                                  ;in: after relocation,
 23036                                  ;    ax = 4b00h - load and execute the program dos function.
 23037                                  ;    ds = confbot. segment of config.sys file image
 23038                                  ;    es = sysinitseg. segment of sysinit module itself.
 23039                                  ;    ds:dx = pointer to asciiz string of the path,filename to be executed.
 23040                                  ;    es:bx = pointer to a parameter block for load.
 23041                                  ;    SI_end (byte) - offset vaule of end of sysinit module label
 23042                                  ;    bigsize (word) - # of word from confbot to SI_end.
 23043                                  ;    chksum (word) - sum of every byte from confbot to SI_end in a
 23044                                  ;			word boundary moduler form.
 23045                                  ;    sysinit_ptr (dword ptr) - return address to sysinit module.
 23046                                  ;
 23047                                  ;note: sysinit should save necessary registers and when the control is back
 23048                                  
 23049                                  	; 24/10/2022
 23050                                  	; (SYSINIT:115Ch for MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 23051                                  sysinit_base:				
 23052 0000113B 2E8C166200              	mov	[cs:sysinit_base_ss],ss	; save stack
 23053 00001140 2E89266400              	mov	[cs:sysinit_base_sp],sp	
 23054 00001145 CD21                    	int	21h			; load/exec dos call.
 23055 00001147 2E8E166200              	mov	ss,[cs:sysinit_base_ss]	; restore stack
 23056 0000114C 2E8B266400              	mov	sp,[cs:sysinit_base_sp]
 23057 00001151 1F                      	pop	ds			; restore confbot seg
 23058 00001152 07                      	pop	es			; restore sysinitseg
 23059 00001153 7216                    	jc	short sysinit_base_end	; load/exec function failed.
 23060                                  					; at this time,i don't have to worry about
 23061                                  					; that sysinit module has been broken or not.
 23062 00001155 E81800                  	call	sum_up			; otherwise,check if it is good.
 23063 00001158 263906[DA02]            	cmp	[es:checksum],ax
 23064 0000115D 740C                    	je	short sysinit_base_end

 23078                                  		; DS:DX -> string terminated by "$"
 23079                                  
 23080                                  	; 30/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.2
 23081                                  stall:
 23082                                  	; 24/10/2022

 23084                                  	; 11/12/2022

 23097                                  ;in:   es - sysinitseg.
 23098                                  ;out:  ax - result
 23099                                  ;
 23100                                  ;remark: since this routine will only check starting from "locstack" to the end of
 23101                                  ;	 sysinit segment,the data area, and the current stack area are not
 23102                                  ;	 coverd. in this sense,this check sum routine only gives a minimal
 23103                                  ;	 gaurantee to be safe.
 23104                                  ;
 23105                                  ;first sum up confbot seg.
 23106                                  
 23107 00001170 1E                      	push	ds

 23247                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 23248                                  ; procedure : GetBufferAddr
 23249                                  ;
 23250                                  ;	      Gets the buffer address either in HMA or in Lo Mem
 23251                                  ;
 23252                                  ; returns in es:di the buffer adress
 23253                                  ; returns NZ if allocated in HMA
 23254                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 23255                                  
 23256                                  	; 25/10/2022 
 23257                                  GetBufferAddr:
 23258 00001216 53                      	push	bx
 23259 00001217 52                      	push	dx
 23260 00001218 2EA1[9D02]              	mov	ax, [cs:singlebuffersize]
 23261 0000121C 2EF726[9902]            	mul	word [cs:buffers]
 23262                                  	;add	ax,0Fh
 23263 00001221 83C00F                  	add	ax,15 
 23264                                  	; 02/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 23265                                  	;and	ax,~15	; 0FFF0h	; para round
 23266                                  	; 12/12/2022
 23267 00001224 24F0                    	and	al,~15	; 0F0h
 23268 00001226 89C3                    	mov	bx,ax
 23269 00001228 B8024A                  	mov	ax,4A02h
 23270                                  	;mov	ax,((multMULT<<8)+multMULTALLOCHMA)
 23271 0000122B CD2F                    	int	2Fh	; DOS 5+ - ALLOCATE HMA SPACE
 23272                                  			;     AX = 4A02h
 23273                                  			;     BX = number of bytes
 23274                                  			; Return:
 23275                                  			;     ES:DI -> start of allocated HMA block or FFFFh:FFFFh
 23276                                  			;     BX = number of bytes actually allocated
 23277                                  			;	   (rounded up to next paragraph)
 23278                                  			; Notes:
 23279                                  			;     this call is not valid unless DOS is loaded in the HMA
 23280                                  			;     (DOS=HIGH)
 23281                                  
 23282 0000122D 83FFFF                  	cmp	di,0FFFFh
 23283 00001230 7506                    	jne	short got_hma
 23284                                  	
 23285                                  	;mov	di,0			; dont xor di,di Z flag needed
 23286                                  	; 05/09/2023
 23287                                  	; zf=1
 23288 00001232 47                      	inc	di ; 0FFFFh -> 0
 23289                                  	; zf=1
 23290                                  	
 23291                                  	;zf=1
 23292                                  	;xor	di,di	; 25/10/2022
 23293                                  	;zf=1
 23294 00001233 2E8E06[6403]            	mov	es,[cs:memhi]
 23295                                  got_hma:
 23296 00001238 5A                      	pop	dx
 23297 00001239 5B                      	pop	bx
 23298 0000123A C3                      	retn

 23328                                  ; ======================================================================
 23329                                  ; MSSTACK initialization routine - MSDOS 6.0 - SYSDINIT1.ASM - 1991
 23330                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 23331                                  ; 27/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 23332                                  
 23333                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 23334                                  ; ibmstack initialization routine.
 23335                                  ;
 23336                                  ;	to follow the standard interrupt sharing scheme, msstack.asm
 23337                                  ;	has been modified. this initialization routine also has to
 23338                                  ;	be modified because for the interrupt level 7 and 15, firstflag
 23339                                  ;	should be set to signal that this interrupt handler is the
 23340                                  ;	first handler hooked to this interrupt vector.
 23341                                  ;	we determine this by looking at the instruction pointed by
 23342                                  ;	this vector. if it is iret, then this handler should be the
 23343                                  ;	first one. in our case, only the interrupt vector 77h is the
 23344                                  ;	interrupt level 15. (we don't hook interrupt level 7.)
 23345                                  ;
 23346                                  ;	the followings are mainly due to m.r.t; ptm fix of p886 12/3/86
 23347                                  ;	some design changes are needed to the above interrupt sharing
 23348                                  ;	method. the above sharing scheme assumes that 1). interrupt
 23349                                  ;	sharing is never done on levels that have bios support. 2). "phantom"
 23350                                  ;	interrupts would only be generated on levels 7 and 15.
 23351                                  ;	these assumptions are not true any more. we have to use the firstflag
 23352                                  ;	for every level of interrupt. we will set the firstflag on the following
 23353                                  ;	conditions:
 23354                                  ;
 23355                                  ;	 a.	 if the cs portion of the vector is 0000, then "first"
 23356                                  ;	 b. else if cs:ip points to valid shared header, then not "first"
 23357                                  ;	 c. else if cs:ip points to an iret, then "first"
 23358                                  ;	 d. else if cs:ip points to dummy, then "first"
 23359                                  ;
 23360                                  ;	where dummy is - the cs portion must be f000, and the ip portion must
 23361                                  ;	be equal to the value at f000:ff01. this location is the initial value
 23362                                  ;	from vector_table for interrupt 7, one of the preserved addresses in all
 23363                                  ;	the bioses for all of the machines.
 23364                                  ;
 23365                                  ;	system design group requests bios to handle the phantom interrupts.
 23366                                  ;
 23367                                  ;	the "phantom" interrupt is an illegal interrupt such as an interrupt
 23368                                  ;	produced by the bogus adapter card even without interrupt request is
 23369                                  ;	set.  more specifically, 1). the 8259 has a feature when running in
 23370                                  ;	edge triggered mode to latch a pulse and present the interrupt when
 23371                                  ;	the processor indicates interrupt acknowledge (inta). the interrupt
 23372                                  ;	pulse was exist at the time of inta to get a "phantom" interrupt.
 23373                                  ;	2). or, this is caused by adapter cards placing a glitch on the
 23374                                  ;	interrupt line.
 23375                                  ;
 23376                                  ;	to handle those "phantom" interrupts, the main stack code will check
 23377                                  ;	the own firstflag, and if it is not "first" (which means the forward
 23378                                  ;	pointer points to the legal shared interrupt handler), then pass the
 23379                                  ;	control. if it is the first, then the following action should be
 23380                                  ;	taken. we don't have to implement skack logic in this case.
 23381                                  ;
 23382                                  ;	to implement this logic, we rather choose a simple method.
 23383                                  ;	if ont of the above "firstflag" conditions is met, we are not
 23384                                  ;	going to hook this interrupt vector. the reason is if the original
 23385                                  ;	vector points to "iret" and do nothing, we don't need
 23386                                  ;	to implement the stack logic for it. this will simplify implementation
 23387                                  ;	while maintaining compatibility with the old version of dos.
 23388                                  ;	this implies that in the main stack code, there might be a stack code
 23389                                  ;	that will never be used, a dead code.
 23390                                  ;
 23391                                  ;in - cs, ds -> sysinitseg, es -> relocated stack code & data.
 23392                                  
 23393                                  	; 25/10/2022 - Retro DOS 4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 23394                                  	; (SYSINIT:1287h)
 23395                                  
 23396                                  	; 14/12/2022

 24199 0000142C 26C51C                  	lds	bx,[es:si]
 24200 0000142F 1E                      	push	ds
 24201 00001430 5A                      	pop	dx
 24202                                  		
 24203                                  	;cmp	dx,0
 24204                                  	;je	short int_xx_first
 24205                                  	; 05/09/2023

 24207 00001433 741E                    	jz	short int_xx_first
 24208                                  	
 24209 00001435 803FCF                  	cmp	byte [bx],0CFh
 24210 00001438 7419                    	je	short int_xx_first
 24211                                  	
 24212 0000143A 817F064B42              	cmp	word [bx+6],424Bh
 24213 0000143F 7411                    	je	short int_xx_not_first
 24214                                  	
 24215 00001441 81FA00F0                	cmp	dx,0F000h
 24216 00001445 750B                    	jne	short int_xx_not_first
 24217

 24219                                  	;push	dx
 24220                                  	;mov	dx,0F000h
 24221 00001448 8EC2                    	mov	es,dx
 24222 0000144A 263B1E01FF              	cmp	bx,[es:0FF01h]
 24223                                        	;pop	dx

 24225 00001450 7401                    	je	short int_xx_first

 24231 00001454 C3                      	retn
 24232                                  
 24233                                  ;%endif

 24235                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 24236                                  ; 27/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 24237                                  
 24238                                  ; 25/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 24239                                  ; (SYSINIT:1610h)
 24240                                  
 24241                                  ; 13/04/2024 - Retro DOS v4.2 (Modified MSDOS 6.22 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 24242                                  ; (SYSINIT:1745h)
 24243                                  
 24244                                  new_init_loop:
 24245                                  
 24246                                  ;input: si=ofset into vector table of the particular int vector being adjusted
 24247                                  ;	bx=ds:offset of oldxx, where will be saved the pointer to original owner
 24248                                  ;	dx=ds:offset of intxx, the new interrupt handler
 24249                                  ;	di=offset value of int19old&aa variable in bios.
 24250                                  ;	es=zero, segid of vector table
 24251                                  ;	ds=relocated stack code segment
 24252                                  
 24253                                  ; 13/04/2024
 24254                                  %if 0
 24255                                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;remember offset in vector
 24256                                  	mov	[bx],ax			; to original owner in ds
 24257                                  	mov	ax,[es:si+2]		;remember segid in vector
 24258                                  	mov	[bx+2],ax		; to original owner in ds
 24259                                  
 24260                                  	push	ds
 24261                                  	;;mov	ax,Bios_Data ; 70h
 24262                                  	;mov	ax,KERNEL_SEGMENT ; 70h
 24263                                  	; 21/10/2022
 24264                                  	mov	ax,DOSBIODATASEG ; 0070h
 24265                                  	mov	ds,ax			;set int19oldxx value in bios for
 24266                                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;int 19 handler
 24267                                  	mov	[di],ax
 24268                                  	mov	ax,[es:si+2]
 24269                                  	mov	[di+2],ax
 24270                                  	pop	ds
 24271                                  %else
 24272                                  	; 13/04/2024 - Retro DOS v4.2
 24273 00001455 1E                      	push	ds
 24274 00001456 268B4402                	mov	ax,[es:si+2]		;remember segid in vector
 24275 0000145A 894702                  	mov	[bx+2],ax		; to original owner in ds
 24276 0000145D 50                      	push	ax
 24277 0000145E 268B04                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;remember offset in vector
 24278 00001461 8907                    	mov	[bx],ax			; to original owner in ds
 24279 00001463 50                      	push	ax
 24280 00001464 B87000                  	mov	ax,DOSBIODATASEG ; 0070h
 24281 00001467 8ED8                    	mov	ds,ax			;set int19oldxx value in bios for
 24282 00001469 58                      	pop	ax			;int 19 handler
 24283 0000146A 8905                    	mov	[di],ax
 24284 0000146C 58                      	pop	ax
 24285 0000146D 894502                  	mov	[di+2],ax
 24286 00001470 1F                      	pop	ds
 24287                                  %endif
 24288 00001471 268914                  	mov	[es:si],dx  	;set vector to point to new int handler
 24289 00001474 268C5C02                	mov	[es:si+2],ds
 24290 00001478 C3                      	retn

 24579                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24580                                  ; << Control field definition  >>
 24581                                  ;
 24582                                  ;
 24583                                  ;CONTROL   LABEL   BYTE
 24584                                  ;	   DW	   MATCH_FLAGS	   ; CONTROLS TYPE MATCHED
 24585                                  ;				   ; 8000H=NUMERIC VALUE, (VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 24586                                  ;				   ; 4000H=SIGNED NUMERIC VALUE (VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 24587                                  ;				   ; 2000H=SIMPLE STRING(VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 24588                                  ;				   ; 1000H=DATE STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 24589                                  ;				   ; 0800H=TIME STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 24590                                  ;				   ; 0400H=COMPLEX LIST (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 24591                                  ;				   ; 0200H=FILE SPEC (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 24592                                  ;				   ; 0100H=DRIVE ONLY (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 24593                                  ;				   ; 0080H=QUOTED STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 24594                                  ;				   ; 0010H=IGNORE ":" AT END IN MATCH
 24595                                  ;				   ; 0002H=REPEATS ALLOWED
 24596                                  ;				   ; 0001H=OPTIONAL
 24597                                  ;	   DW	   FUNCTION_FLAGS
 24598                                  ;				   ; 0001H=CAP RESULT BY FILE TABLE
 24599                                  ;				   ; 0002H=CAP RESULT BY CHAR TABLE
 24600                                  ;				   ; 0010H=REMOVE ":" AT END
 24601                                  ; (tm10)			   ; 0020H=colon is not necessary for switch
 24602                                  ;	   DW	   RESULT	   ; RESULT BUFFER
 24603                                  ;	   DW	   VALUES	   ; VALUE LISTS
 24604                                  ;	   DB	   nid		   ; NUMBER OF KEYWORD/SWITCH SYNONYMS IN FOLLOWING LIST
 24605                                  ;	   DB	   "...",0         ; IF n >0, KEYWORD 1
 24606                                  ;	   :
 24607                                  ;
 24608                                  ;Note:
 24609                                  ;    - The MATCH_FLAG is bit significant. You can set, for example, TIME bit and
 24610                                  ;      DATE bit simalteniously.
 24611                                  ;
 24612                                  ;      The parser examins each bit along with the following priority.
 24613                                  ;
 24614                                  ;      COMPLEX -> DATE -> TIME -> NUMERIC VAL -> SIGNED NUMERIC VAL -> DRIVE ->
 24615                                  ;      FILE SPEC -> SIMPLE STRING.
 24616                                  ;
 24617                                  ;    - When the FUNCTION_FLAG is 0001 or 0002, the STRING pointed to by a pointer
 24618                                  ;      in the result buffer is capitalized.
 24619                                  ;
 24620                                  ;    - Match_Flags 0001H and 0002H have meaning only for the positional.
 24621                                  ;
 24622                                  ;    - The "...",0 (bottom most line) does require '=' or '/'. When you need a
 24623                                  ;      switch, for example, '/A', then STRING points to;
 24624                                  ;
 24625                                  ;			DB    1 	; number of following synonyms
 24626                                  ;			DB   '/A',0
 24627                                  ;
 24628                                  ;      When you need a keyword, for example, 'CODEPAGE=', then "...",0 will be;
 24629                                  ;
 24630                                  ;			DB    1 	; number of following synonyms
 24631                                  ;			DB   'CODEPAGE=',0
 24632                                  ;
 24633                                  ;    - "..." must consist of upper case characters only because the parser
 24634                                  ;      performs pattern matching after converting input to upper case (by
 24635                                  ;      using the current country upper case table)
 24636                                  ;
 24637                                  ;    - One "..." can contain only one switch or keyword. If you need, for
 24638                                  ;      example /A and /B, the format will be;
 24639                                  ;
 24640                                  ;			DB    2 	; number of following synonyms
 24641                                  ;			DB    '/A',0
 24642                                  ;			DB    '/B',0
 24643                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24644                                  
 24645                                  ;**** Match_Flags
 24646                                  
 24647                                  _$P_Num_Val	   equ	8000h		;AN000; Numeric Value
 24648                                  _$P_SNum_Val	   equ	4000h		;AN000; Signed numeric value
 24649                                  _$P_Simple_S	   equ	2000h		;AN000; Simple string
 24650                                  _$P_Date_S	   equ	1000h		;AN000; Date string
 24651                                  _$P_Time_S	   equ	0800h		;AN000; Time string
 24652                                  _$P_Cmpx_S	   equ	0400h		;AN000; Complex string
 24653                                  _$P_File_Spc	   equ	0200h		;AN000; File Spec
 24654                                  _$P_Drv_Only	   equ	0100h		;AN000; Drive Only
 24655                                  _$P_Qu_String	   equ	0080h		;AN000; Quoted string
 24656                                  _$P_Ig_Colon	   equ	0010h		;AN000; Ignore colon at end in match
 24657                                  _$P_Repeat	   equ	0002h		;AN000; Repeat allowed
 24658                                  _$P_Optional	   equ	0001h		;AN000; Optional
 24659                                  
 24660                                  ;**** Function flags
 24661                                  
 24662                                  _$P_CAP_File	   equ	0001h		;AN000; CAP result by file table
 24663                                  _$P_CAP_Char	   equ	0002h		;AN000; CAP result by character table
 24664                                  _$P_Rm_Colon	   equ	0010h		;AN000; Remove ":" at the end
 24665                                  _$P_colon_is_not_necessary equ 0020h	;AN000;(tm10) /+10 and /+:10
 24666                                  
 24667                                  ;-------------------------------- Control block structure
 24668                                  struc _$P_Control_Blk
 24669 00000000 ????                     .Match_Flag:	 resw 1		;AN000; Controls type matched
 24670 00000002 ????                     .Function_Flag: resw 1		;AN000; Function should be taken
 24671 00000004 ????                     .Result_Buf:	 resw 1		; Result buffer address
 24672 00000006 ????                     .Value_List:	 resw 1		;AN000; Value list address
 24673 00000008 ??                       .nid:		 resb 1		;AN000; # of keyword/SW synonyms
 24674 00000009 ??                       .KEYorSW:	 resb 1		;AN000; keyword or sw
 24675                                  endstruc
 24676                                  
 24677                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24678                                  ; << Value List Definition >>
 24679                                  ;
 24680                                  ;VALUES 	LABEL	BYTE
 24681                                  ;		DB	nval			; NUMBER OF VALUE DEFINITIONS (0 - 3)
 24682                                  ;	     +-
 24683                                  ;	     |	DB	nrng			; NUMBER OF RANGES
 24684                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF RANGE MATCHED
 24685                                  ;	     | +DD	X,Y			; RANGE OF VALUES
 24686                                  ;	     |	:
 24687                                  ;	     |	DB	nnval			; NUMBER OF CHOICES
 24688                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF NUMBER CHOICE MATCHED
 24689                                  ;	     | +DD	VALUE			; SPECIFIC CHOICE IF NUMBER
 24690                                  ;	     |	:
 24691                                  ;	     |	DB	nstrval 		; NUMBER OF CHOICES
 24692                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF STRING CHOICE MATCHED
 24693                                  ;	     | +DW	STRING			; SPECIFIC CHOICE IF STING
 24694                                  ;	     +-	:
 24695                                  ;
 24696                                  ;STRING 	DB	"...",0                 ; ASCIIZ STRING IMAGE
 24697                                  ;
 24698                                  ;Note:
 24699                                  ;    - ITEM_TAG must not be 0FFH, which will be used in the result buffer
 24700                                  ;      when no choice lists are provided.
 24701                                  ;
 24702                                  ;    - STRING must consist of upper case characters only because the parser
 24703                                  ;      performs pattern matching after converting input to upper case (by
 24704                                  ;      using the current country upper case table)
 24705                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24706                                  
 24707                                  _$P_nval_None	   equ	0		;AN000; no value list ID
 24708                                  _$P_nval_Range	   equ	1		;AN000; range list ID
 24709                                  _$P_nval_Value	   equ	2		;AN000; value list ID
 24710                                  _$P_nval_String	   equ	3		;AN000; string list ID
 24711                                  _$P_Len_Range	   equ	9		;AN000; Length of a range choice(two DD plus one DB)
 24712                                  _$P_Len_Value	   equ	5		;AN000; Length of a value choice(one DD plus one DB)
 24713                                  _$P_Len_String	   equ	3		;AN000; Length of a string choice(one DW plus one DB)
 24714                                  _$P_No_nrng	   equ	0		;AN000; (tm07) no nrng. nnval must not be 0.

 24717 00000000 ??                       .NumofList: resb 1			;AN000; number of following choice
 24718 00000001 ????                     .Val_XL:    resw 1			;AN000; lower word of value
 24719 00000003 ????                     .Val_XH:    resw 1			;AN000; higher word of value
 24720 00000005 ????                     .Val_YL:    resw 1			;AN000; lower word of another value
 24721 00000007 ????                     .Val_YH:    resw 1			;AN000; higher word of another value
 24722                                  endstruc
 24723                                  
 24724                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24725                                  ; << Result Buffer Definition  >>
 24726                                  ;
 24727                                  ;RESULT 	LABEL	BYTE			; BELOW FILLED IN FOR DEFAULTS
 24728                                  ;		DB	type			; TYPE RETURNED: 0=RESERVED,
 24729                                  ;						;	1=NUMBER, 2=LIST INDEX,
 24730                                  ;						;	3=STRING, 4=COMPLEX,
 24731                                  ;						;	5=FILESPEC, 6=DRIVE
 24732                                  ;						;	7=DATE, 8=TIME
 24733                                  ;						;	9=QUOTED STRING
 24734                                  ;		DB	ITEM_TAG		; MATCHED ITEM TAG
 24735                                  ;
 24736                                  ;		dw	synonym@		; es:@ points to found SYNONYM if provided.
 24737                                  ;
 24738                                  ;            +-
 24739                                  ;	    | DD	n			; VALUE IF NUMBER
 24740                                  ;	    | or
 24741                                  ;	    |	DW	i			; INDEX (OFFSET) INTO VALUE LIST
 24742                                  ;	    |					; (ES presents Segment address)
 24743                                  ;	    | or
 24744                                  ;	    |	DD	STRING			; OFFSET OF STRING VALUE
 24745                                  ;	    | or
 24746                                  ;	    |	DB	drv			; DRIVE NUMBER (1-A, 2-B,..., 26-Z)
 24747                                  ;	    | or
 24748                                  ;	    |	DW	YEAR	   ;(1980-2099)  IN CASE OF DATE
 24749                                  ;	    |	DB	MONTH	   ;(1-12)	 Note: Range check is not performed.
 24750                                  ;	    |	DB	DATE	   ;(1-31)	       0 is filled when the corresponding field was not specified.
 24751                                  ;	    | or
 24752                                  ;	    |	DB	HOUR	   ;(0-23)	  IN CASE OF TIME
 24753                                  ;	    |	DB	MINUTES    ;(0-59)	  Note: Range check is not performed .
 24754                                  ;	    |	DB	SECONDS    ;(0-59)		0 is filled when the corresponding field was not specified .
 24755                                  ;	    |	DB	HUNDREDTHS ;(0-99)
 24756                                  ;	    +-
 24757                                  ;
 24758                                  ;
 24759                                  ;Note: ITEM_TAG is 0FFH when the caller does not specify the choice
 24760                                  ;      list.
 24761                                  ;
 24762                                  ;      YEAR: If the input value for the year is less than 100, parser
 24763                                  ;	     adds 1900 to it.  For example, when 87 is input to parser for
 24764                                  ;	     the year value, he returns 1987.
 24765                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 24890                                  ;***********************************************************************
 24891                                  ; SysParse;
 24892                                  ;
 24893                                  ;  Function : Parser Entry
 24894                                  ;
 24895                                  ;  Input: DS:SI -> command line
 24896                                  ;	  ES:DI -> parameter block
 24897                                  ;	  cs -> psdata.inc
 24898                                  ;	  CX = operand ordinal
 24899                                  ;
 24900                                  ;	  Note:  ES is the segment containing all the control blocks defined
 24901                                  ;		 by the caller, except for the DOS COMMAND line parms, which
 24902                                  ;		 is in DS.
 24903                                  ;
 24904                                  ;  Output: CY = 1   error of caller, means invalid parameter block or
 24905                                  ;		    invalid value list. But this parser does NOT implement
 24906                                  ;		    this feature. Therefore CY always zero.
 24907                                  ;
 24908                                  ;	   CY = 0   AX = return code
 24909                                  ;		    BL = terminated delimiter code
 24910                                  ;		    CX = new operand ordinal
 24911                                  ;		    SI = set past scaned operand
 24912                                  ;		    DX = selected result buffer
 24913                                  ;
 24914                                  ; Use:	_$P_Skip_Delim, _$P_Chk_EOL, _$P_Chk_Delim, _$P_Chk_DBCS
 24915                                  ;	_$P_Chk_Swtch, _$P_Chk_Pos_Control, _$P_Chk_Key_Control
 24916                                  ;	_$P_Chk_Sw_Control, _$P_Fill_Result
 24917                                  ;
 24918                                  ; Vars: _$P_Ordinal(RW), _$P_RC(RW), _$P_SI_Save(RW), _$P_DX(R), _$P_Terminator(R)
 24919                                  ;	_$P_SaveSI_Cmpx(W), _$P_Flags(RW), _$P_Found_SYNONYM(R), _$P_Save_EOB(W)
 24920                                  ;

 27067                                  ; _$P_Chk_Switch;
 27068                                  ;
 27069                                  ; Function: Check if AL is the switch character not in first position of
 27070                                  ;	    _$P_STRING_BUF
 27071                                  ;
 27072                                  ; Input:    AL = character code
 27073                                  ;	    BX = current pointer within _$P_String_Buf
 27074                                  ;	    SI =>next char on command line (following the one in AL)
 27075                                  ;
 27076                                  ; Output:   CF = 1 (set)if AL is switch character, and not in first
 27077                                  ;		 position, and has no chance of being part of a date string,
 27078                                  ;		 i.e. should be treated as a delimiter.
 27079                                  
 27080                                  ;	    CF = 0 (reset, cleared) if AL is not a switch char, is in the first
 27081                                  ;		 position, or is a slash but may be part of a date string, i.e.
 27082                                  ;		 should not be treated as a delimiter.
 27083                                  ;
 27084                                  ; Vars:  _$P_Terminator(W)
 27085                                  
 27086                                  ; Use:	 _$P_0099
 27087                                  ;***********************************************************************
 27088                                  
 27089                                  _$P_Chk_Switch:
 27090                                  	;;lea	bp,[cs:_$P_STRING_BUF]	;AN020;AC034
 27091                                  	;lea	bp,[_$P_STRING_BUF]	;BP=OFFSET of _$P_String_Buf even in group addressing
 27092                                  	; 08/07/2023
 27093 00001C9B BD[BB14]                	mov	bp,_$P_STRING_BUF
 27094                                  
 27095                                  ;	.IF <BX NE BP> THEN		;AN020;IF not first char THEN
 27096 00001C9E 39EB                    	cmp	bx,bp			;AN000;
 27097 00001CA0 7406                    	je	short _$P_STRUC_L2	;AN000;
 27098                                  
 27099                                  ;	.IF <AL EQ _$P_Switch> THEN	;AN020;otherwise see if a slash
 27100 00001CA2 3C2F                    	cmp	al,_$P_Switch		;AN000;
 27101 00001CA4 750C                    	jne	short _$P_STRUC_L5 	;AN000;
 27102                                  
 27103 00001CA6 F9                      	stc				;AN020;not in first position and is slash
 27104                                  	;jmp     short _$P_STRUC_L1	;AN000;
 27105                                  	; 12/12/2022
 27106 00001CA7 C3                      	retn
 27107                                  
 27108                                  ; 12/12/2022
 27109                                  ;_$P_STRUC_L5:				;AN000;
 27110                                  ;	CLC				;AN020;not a slash
 27111                                  ;;	    .ENDIF			;AN020;
 27112                                  ;;	.ELSE				;AN020;is first char in the buffer, ZF=0
 27113                                  ;	jmp	short _$P_STRUC_L1	;AN000;
 27114                                  
 27115                                  _$P_STRUC_L2:				;AN000;
 27116                                  ;	.IF <AL EQ _$P_Switch> THEN	;AN020;
 27117 00001CA8 3C2F                    	cmp     al,_$P_Switch		;AN000;
 27118 00001CAA 7506                    	jne	short _$P_STRUC_L12	;AN000;
 27119                                  
 27120 00001CAC 2E800E[B214]40          	or	byte [cs:_$P_Flags2],_$P_SW ;AN020 ;AC034;;could be valid switch, first char and is slash
 27121                                  ;	.ENDIF				;AN020;
 27122                                  
 27123                                  	; 12/12/2022
 27124                                  	; cf=0
 27125                                  	;retn
 27126                                  
 27127                                  _$P_STRUC_L5:
 27128                                  	; 12/12/2022
 27129                                  _$P_STRUC_L12:				;AN000;
 27130 00001CB2 F8                      	clc				;AN020;CF=0 indicating first char

 27780                                  ;include	highvar.inc	; devicehigh variables (used by loadhigh also)
 27781                                  
 27782                                  ; 30/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 27783                                  ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 27784                                  
 27785                                  ;   Module:   HIGHVAR.INC - Data common to LOADHIGH and DEVICEHIGH, res seg
 27786                                  ;
 27787                                  ;   Date:     May 14, 1992
 27788                                  ;
 27789                                  ;******************************************************************************
 27790                                  ;
 27791                                  ;   Modification log:
 27792                                  ;
 27793                                  ;     DATE    WHO      DESCRIPTION
 27794                                  ;   --------  -------  --------------------------------------------------------
 27795                                  ;   05/14/92  t-richj  Original
 27796                                  ;   06/21/92  t-richj  Final revisions before check-in
 27797                                  ;
 27798                                  ;******************************************************************************
 27799                                  ;
 27800                                  ; There are two primary definitions which need to be made, selectively, before
 27801                                  ; this include file should be used.  These are:
 27802                                  ;    HV_Extern - If this has been defined, variables for this module will be
 27803                                  ;                declared as external.  Otherwise, variables will be declared
 27804                                  ;                public, as well as defined, here.  LoadHigh declares HV_Extern
 27805                                  ;                in stub.asm and loadhi.asm, and does not declare it in
 27806                                  ;                rdata.asm... DeviceHigh does not declare HV_Extern anywhere
 27807                                  ;                (as only one module, sysconf.asm, includes this file).
 27808                                  ;    HV_LoadHigh - This should be defined when this module is going into
 27809                                  ;                  command.com, for LoadHigh.  All of loadhi.asm, stub.asm and
 27810                                  ;                  rdata.asm define this, while io.sys' sysconf.asm does not.
 27811                                  ;
 27812                                  ;******************************************************************************
 27813                                  
 27814                                  ; To keep track of which UMBs were specified on the DH/LH command lines, and
 27815                                  ; to keep track of the minimum sizes given for each, there're two arrays kept
 27816                                  ; in { IO.SYS: sysinitseg / COMMAND.COM: DATARES }... each is MAXUMB elements
 27817                                  ; big.  16 should be around 14 too many for most users, so there's no expected
 27818                                  ; space problem (it's just such a nice round number, eh?).
 27819                                  
 27820                                  MAXUMB	equ	16
 27821                                  
 27822                                  ; Memory elements owned by the system are marked as PSP address 8 in both the
 27823                                  ; USA and Japan; Japanese systems also use 9 under more bizzarre conditions.
 27824                                  
 27825                                  FreePSPOwner	equ	0	; Free MCBs all have an owner PSP address of 0
 27826                                  SystemPSPOwner	equ	8
 27827                                  ;JapanPSPOwner	equ	9
 27828                                  
 27829                                  ; for LoadHigh and DeviceHigh:
 27830                                  ;
 27831                                  ;	fInHigh - Is set to 1 during HideUMBs(), and back to zero in
 27832                                  ;	          UnHideUMBs().
 27833                                  ;	fUmbTiny - Is set to 1 iff the user has specified /S on the command-
 27834                                  ;	           line.
 27835                                  ;	SegLoad - Segment address for first UMB specified; set automatically.
 27836                                  ;	UmbLoad - The load UMB number; for example, this is 3 if the user has
 27837                                  ;	          given a command-line like "/L:3,500;4"
 27838                                  ;	UmbUsed - An array of characters, each of which is 1 iff the UMB
 27839                                  ;	          matching its index number was specified on the command-line;
 27840                                  ;	          for example, after "/L:3,500;4;7", UmbUsed[3], [4] and [7]
 27841                                  ;	          will be set to 1.  All others will be set to 0.
 27842                                  ;	UmbSize - An array of words, each of which is interpereted as a size
 27843                                  ;	          specified by the user for a UMB (in the above example, all
 27844                                  ;	          elements would be zero save UmbSize[3], which would be 500.
 27845                                  ;	fm_umb - Set to the old UMB link-state (0x80 or 0x00)
 27846                                  ;	fm_strat - Set to the old memory-allocation strategy (0$00000???)
 27847                                  ;	fm_argc  - Number of arguments received by ParseVar() (see ParseVar()
 27848                                  ;	           for details).
 27849                                  
 27850 00001F00 00                      fInHigh:  db	0
 27851 00001F01 00                      fUmbTiny: db	0
 27852 00001F02 0000                    SegLoad:  dw	0
 27853 00001F04 00                      UmbLoad:  db	0
 27854 00001F05 00<rep 10h>             UmbUsed:  times MAXUMB db 0 ; times 16 db 0  ; db 16 dup(?)
 27855 00001F15 0000<rep 10h>           UmbSize:  times MAXUMB dw 0 ; times 16 dw 0  ; dw 16 dup(?)
 27856 00001F35 00                      fm_umb:   db	0
 27857 00001F36 00                      fm_strat: db	0
 27858 00001F37 00                      fm_argc:  db	0	
 27859                                  
 27860                                  ; UmbLoad is set to UNSPECIFED, below, until /L:umb is read; at which point
 27861                                  ; UmbLoad is set to the UMB number given.
 27862                                  
 27863                                  UNSPECIFIED	equ	-1
 27864                                  
 27865                                  ;%endif ; 27/10/2022
 27866                                  
 27867                                  ;****************************************************************** RICHID ****
 27868                                  
 27869                                  ; 30/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0 (MSDOS 6.0, SYSCONF.ASM)
 27870                                  ; ((MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS -> SYNINIT:22BAh))
 27871                                  
 27872                                  ; 27/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS)
 27873                                  ; (SYSINIT:212Bh)	
 27874                                  
 27875                                  		;public	DevEntry
 27876                                  
 27877 00001F38 0000                    DevSize:	dw	0	; size of the device driver being loaded(paras)

 28177 0000205B 86C4                            xchg    al,ah                   ; supposed to be there, the next
 28178 0000205D A3[AF02]                        mov     [linecount],ax          ; getchr call will get the same error
 28179 00002060 58                              pop     ax

 28181                                  ;   HACK: when 4DOS.COM is the shell and it doesn't have an environment from
 28182                                  ;   which to obtain its original program name, it grovels through all of
 28183                                  ;   memory to find the filename that was used to exec it; it wants to find
 28184                                  ;   the SHELL= line in the in-memory copy of CONFIG.SYS, and it knows that
 28185                                  ;   sysinit converts the SHELL= keyword to an 'S', so it expects to find an 'S'
 28186                                  ;   immediately before the filename, but since we are now storing line # info
 28187                                  ;   in the config.sys memory image, 4DOS fails to find the 'S' in the right
 28188                                  ;   spot.
 28189                                  ;
 28190                                  ;   So, on the final pass of CONFIG.SYS, copy the command code (eg, 'S')
 28191                                  ;   over the line number info, since we no longer need that info anyway. This
 28192                                  ;   relies on the fact that getchr leaves ES:SI pointing to the last byte
 28193                                  ;   retrieved.
 28194                                  ;

 30129                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 30130                                  ; setting internal stack parameters
 30131                                  ; stacks=m,n where

 30133                                  ;	n is the stack size (range 32 to 512 bytes,default 128)
 30134                                  ; j.k. 5/5/86: stacks=0,0 implies no stack installation.

 30137                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 30138                                  
 30139                                  ;**************************************************************************
 30140                                  ;									  *
 30141                                  ; function: parse the parameters of stacks= command.			  *
 30142                                  ;	    the minimum value for "number of stacks" and "stack size" is  *
 30143                                  ;	    8 and 32 each.  in the definition of sysparse value list,they *
 30144                                  ;	    are set to 0.  this is for accepting the exceptional case of  *
 30145                                  ;	    stacks=0,0 case (,which means do not install the stack.)	  *
 30146                                  ;	    so,after sysparse is done,we have to check if the entered	  *
 30147                                  ;	    values (stack_count,stack_size) are within the actual range,  *
 30148                                  ;	    (or if "0,0" pair has been entered.)			  *
 30149                                  ; input :								  *
 30150                                  ;	es:si -> parameters in command line.				  *
 30151                                  ; output:								  *
 30152                                  ;	set the variables stack_count,stack_size.			  *
 30153                                  ;									  *
 30154                                  ; subroutines to be called:						  *
 30155                                  ;	sysinit_parse							  *
 30156                                  ; logic:								  *
 30157                                  ; {									  *
 30158                                  ;	set di points to stks_parms;					  *
 30159                                  ;	set dx,cx to 0; 						  *
 30160                                  ;	while (end of command line)					  *
 30161                                  ;	{ sysinit_parse;						  *
 30162                                  ;	  if (no error) then						  *
 30163                                  ;	     { if (cx == 1) then /* first positional = stack count */	  *
 30164                                  ;		   p_stack_count = result_val._$P_picked_val;		  *
 30165                                  ;	       if (cx == 2) then /* second positional = stack size */	  *
 30166                                  ;		   p_stack_size = result_val._$P_picked_val;		  *
 30167                                  ;	     }								  *
 30168                                  ;	  else	/*error exit*/						  *
 30169                                  ;	     error exit;						  *
 30170                                  ;	};								  *
 30171                                  ;	here check p_stack_count,p_stack_size if it meets the condition;  *
 30172                                  ;	if o.k.,then set stack_count,stack_size;			  *

 30174                                  ; };									  *

 31454                                  ;include highload.inc	; Routines for devicehigh parsing, control of HIDDEN
 31455                                  ;include highexit.inc	; umb's, etc
 31456                                  
 31457                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 31458                                  ; HIGHLOAD.INC (MSDOS 6.0 - 1991) 	
 31459                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 31460                                  ; 07/04/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 31461                                  
 31462                                  ;******************************************************************************
 31463                                  ;
 31464                                  ; This file contains routines needed to parse and implement user-given
 31465                                  ; command-line options of the form "/S/L:3,0x500;2;7,127;0x0BE4". InitVar()
 31466                                  ; and Parsevar() are used to parse this data and place it in encoded form into
 31467                                  ; the variables in highvar.inc, for use by the rest of the routines.
 31468                                  ;
 31469                                  ; DeviceHigh accepts this command-line (handled in sysconf.asm, not here):
 31470                                  ;    DEVICEHIGH SIZE=hhhhhh module opts
 31471                                  ; Or, DeviceHigh and LoadHigh accept any of the following:
 31472                                  ;    DH/LH module opts
 31473                                  ;    DH/LH [/S][/L:umb[,size][;umb[,size]]*] module opts
 31474                                  ;    DH/LH [/L:umb[,size][;umb[,size]]*][/S] module opts
 31475                                  ; The initial UMB,SIZE pair designates the module's load address; the remainder
 31476                                  ; of the UMB and SIZE pairs are used to indicate specific UMBs to be left
 31477                                  ; available during the load.
 31478                                  ;
 31479                                  ; When an actual load is ready to be performed, a call to HideUMBs() will
 31480                                  ; temporarily allocate (as owner 8+"HIDDEN  ") all free elements in any
 31481                                  ; upper-memory block which was not specified by the user... in addition, if
 31482                                  ; UMBs were marked to shrink (/S option) to a certain size ("umb,size"), any
 31483                                  ; elements in that umb SAVE the lower-half of the newly-shrunken one are also
 31484                                  ; allocated. After the load, the function UnHideUMBs() (in highexit.inc) will
 31485                                  ; free any UMBs so allocated.
 31486                                  ;
 31487                                  ; When a device driver loads, there is the additional problem of allocating its
 31488                                  ; initial load site; this should be restricted to the first UMB specified on
 31489                                  ; the command-line. The function FreezeUM temporarily allocates all remaining
 31490                                  ; free upper-memory elements (as owner 8+"FROZEN  "), except those in the load
 31491                                  ; UMB. Then the initial allocation may be made, and a call to UnFreeze will
 31492                                  ; return any so-allocated memory elements to FREE, for the true load. Note
 31493                                  ; that UnFreeze leaves HIDDEN elements allocated; it only frees FROZEN ones.
 31494                                  ;
 31495                                  ;******************************************************************************
 31496                                  
 31497                                  SWTCH	equ	'/'		; Switch character
 31498                                  
 31499                                  DOS_CHECK_STRATEGY  equ	5800h	; Int 21h, Func 58h, Svc 0 = check alloc strat
 31500                                  DOS_SET_STRATEGY    equ	5801h	; Int 21h, Func 58h, Svc 1 = set alloc strategy
 31501                                  DOS_CHECK_UMBLINK   equ	5802h	; Int 21h, Func 58h, Svc 2 = check link state
 31502                                  DOS_GET_UMBLINK	    equ 5802h ; 20/04/2019
 31503                                  DOS_SET_UMBLINK     equ	5803h	; Int 21h, Func 58h, Svc 3 = set link state
 31504                                  DOS_GET_DOS_LISTS   equ	  52h	; Int 21h, Func 52h = return list of lists
 31505                                  DOS_UMB_HEAD        equ	  8Ch	; Offset from ES (after func52h) to get UMBHead
 31506                                  
 31507                                  CR	equ	0Dh		; Carriage Return
 31508                                  LF	equ	0Ah		; Line Feed
 31509                                  TAB	equ	09h		; Tab character (^I)
 31510
